newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian soldier to be tried for killing Ogoni man.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian soldier to be tried for killing Ogoni man.

text.p: A Nigerian soldier will face a court martial for allegedly shooting and killing an Ogoni youth, an army commander said on Saturday.
Ogonis are a small tribe in the oil-producing southeastern corner of Nigeria, whose leaders, including author Ken Saro-Wiwa, were hanged in 1995, provoking worldwide condemnation of Nigeria.
State news agency NAN quoted Major Obi Umahi, commander of troops in volatile Ogoniland as saying at a news conference there that the incident occured on July 12.
He said "the soldier acted illegally and without authority by shooting and killing Barika Kogbara," NAN reported.
Umahi commands a task force sent to Ogoniland in 1992 to stop fighting between Ogonis and neighbouring Andoni tribe but which has stayed to enforce security.
Ogoni minority rights campaigners frequently accuse the force of brutalising the strong populution, a charge the authorities deny.
